extracted.intended_audience: Nature authors, reviewers, editors, and the wider research community
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher policy announcing that peer-review files (referees’ reports and author responses) will be published alongside all research articles in Nature, explaining scope, rationale, and implementation details. Useful for authors deciding whether and how to participate and for reviewers understanding how their reports will be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory publication of peer-review files for published research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: From 16 June, new submissions of manuscripts that are published as research articles in Nature will automatically include a link to the reviewers’ reports and author responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This replaces the previous opt-in arrangement and means that, over time, more Nature papers will include a peer-review file. The policy applies automatically to new submissions that are ultimately published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: applies to Nature research articles
rubrics_metrics.description: All new submissions to Nature that are published will be accompanied by referees’ reports and author responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy is specifically for research papers published in Nature (as distinct from e.g., commentary or other non-research content); implementation began on 16 June.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of published peer-review file
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer-review file will include referees’ reports and author responses — the exchanges between the referees and the authors will be accessible to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published material is intended to illuminate the process of producing rigorous science by showing the back-and-forth between reviewers and authors; it does not necessarily include other contributions beyond those exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity preserved unless reviewers choose otherwise
rubrics_metrics.description: The identity of the reviewers will remain anonymous, unless they choose otherwise — as happens now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers retain the option to be named; the default remains anonymity. The announcement emphasises continuity with current practice on anonymity except for reviewer opt-in to being named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility: peer-review files linked and openly available
rubrics_metrics.description: Published research papers will be accompanied by a link to the reviewers’ reports and author responses, making these exchanges accessible to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intention is open access to the peer-review conversation so readers and the wider community can see how a study was critiqued and revised; the link is included with the published paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: increase transparency and build trust in the scientific process
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim in doing so is to open up what many see as the ‘black box’ of science, shedding light on how a research paper is made. This serves to increase transparency and (we hope) to build trust in the scientific process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing peer-review exchanges is framed as a means to make the research-production process clearer to readers and the public and to strengthen trust in published findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of peer reviewers and option to be acknowledged
rubrics_metrics.description: These discussions ... should receive increased recognition, including acknowledgement of the reviewers involved, if they choose to be named.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy supports recognizing reviewers' contributions; reviewer naming remains optional and subject to reviewer choice. The editorial cites trial support for recognizing reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational value for early-career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: For early-career researchers, there is great value in seeing inside a process that is key to their career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making reviewer reports public allows trainees and early-career scientists to learn how peer review operates in practice and how papers are improved through revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science-communication benefit: enriches the story of how results were arrived at
rubrics_metrics.description: Making peer-reviewer reports public also enriches science communication: it’s a chance to add to the ‘story’ of how a result is arrived at, or a conclusion supported, even if it includes only the perspectives of authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published review files can be used to inform public-facing explanations of research, showing the debate and reasoning behind conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review as an integral part of the scientific record because it improves clarity and robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: A published research paper is the result of an extensive conversation between authors and reviewers, guided by editors ... These discussions ... aim to improve a study’s clarity and the robustness of its conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editorial argues that peer-review exchanges should be seen as a crucial part of the scientific record and that publishing them documents how conclusions were strengthened during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based policy change: informed by a trial showing support for recognizing reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Three-year trial shows support for recognizing peer reviewers ... As we have written previously, Nature has offered authors the opportunity to have their peer-review file published alongside their paper. Our colleagues at Nature Communications have been doing so since 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to make peer-review files the default is presented as building on prior trials and other journals’ experience; the editorial uses trial outcomes and precedent as justification for the policy.
